text: Please keep Sister [[Jane]] in your prayers, she is in the hospital this week.

[[Marcus]] asked me to tell y'all thank you for the meals.
Pray for my friend [[Dave]] in the choir, he got some hard news from the doctor.

Pray for [[brenda]] and the whole family as they make arrangements.

Pray for [[Mark]] and [[Joy Patterson]] as they celebrate fifty years of marriage.

Pray for our deacon [[Rick]] and his wife [[Tammy]] as they care for her father.

Happy birthday to [[Nevaeh]], she turns sixteen today.

Congratulations to [[Caleb]] and [[Brittany]] on the birth of baby [[Wyatt]].
Pastor [[Mike]] will be leading youth on Wednesday night.
Thank you to [[Linda]] and the kitchen team for the potluck.

Give [[Kevin]] a hand, he fixed the sound board this week.

If you need a ride to church, call [[Wanda]] in the office.
Shout out to [[Hunter]] and the youth for washing cars yesterday.
The Lord's Supper will be served next Sunday morning.
Our women's Bible study is going through the book of {{Esther}} this fall.
Happy anniversary to [[Ray]] and [[Dawn]], thirty five years.
[[Tiffany]] is collecting coats for the shelter through the end of the month.
Sign the card in the lobby for Mr. [[Gene Caudle]] who turned ninety.
The baptism class meets after service with [[Matthew]] and [[Rebecca Lyle]].
Thanks to [[Oluwaseun]] for running the livestream every week.
Our Sunday school class is studying {{Daniel}} chapter six.
If you're new, stop by and meet [[Jessica]] at the connect center.
Uncle [[Rich]] is grilling for the men's cookout Saturday.
Deacon [[Paul Hester]] will lead our time of prayer.
Granny [[Mae]] made the pound cakes again, so get there early.
We are taking a love offering for the [[Tran]] family this morning.
My wife [[Angela]] and I were broke and scared, and God provided.
I remember sitting in the waiting room with my buddy [[Travis]] and we just prayed.
My granddaddy [[Clyde]] used to read Psalm twenty three every night.
When [[Kayla]] gave her life to Jesus at camp, her whole family came to church.
I had a neighbor named [[Frank]] who never darkened a church door.
[[Jimmy]] told me, Preacher, I've been mad at God for ten years.
My daughter [[Hannah]] asked me why God let her friend get sick.
Our son [[David]] was born three months early and weighed two pounds.
There was a man in my first church, [[Harold Simmons]], who drove the church van for forty years.
My mama [[Doris]] prayed for me every single day I was running from God.
I was in the truck with [[Bobby]] and [[Lynn]] when the call came.
A young lady named [[Destiny]] walked in during the invitation and gave her heart to Christ.
[[Marvin]] said, I don't need church, and three weeks later he was on the front row.
My best friend in high school, [[Jason Pike]], overdosed when we were nineteen.
I'll never forget what Mrs. [[Abernathy]] told me in third grade Sunday school.
Our neighbor [[Elizabeth]] brought us supper every night that week.
I baptized [[Carlos]] and his two boys in the lake behind the church.
My wife's cousin [[Rachel]] works in hospice and she says people die the way they live.
[[Terrence]] and I have been friends since the third grade.
Like {{Peter}}, I denied him, and like {{Peter}}, he restored me.
Our pastor's wife [[Cheryl]] taught me how to pray out loud.
[[Austin]] came up to me after service and said he wanted to be baptized.
I was sitting with [[Gladys]] in the nursing home and she sang Amazing Grace by heart.
Me and [[Darnell]] grew up three houses apart.
My little girl [[Emma]] prays for the dog every night.
Brother [[Joseph]] stood up in the business meeting and confessed his sin.
God used a man named [[Roger Tate]] to lead me to the Lord.
[[Crystal]] was addicted for twelve years and now she leads our recovery group.
My old boss [[Walter]] would say, Son, do it right or don't do it.
When my brother [[James]] came home from Iraq he wasn't the same.
The apostle {{Paul}} wrote to {{Timothy}} from a prison cell in Rome.
{{Moses}} went up the mountain and {{Aaron}} stayed with the people.
{{Mary}} treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart.
{{John}} the Baptist said, He must increase but I must decrease.
Turn with me to {{John}} chapter three, verse sixteen.
{{Peter}} and his brother {{Andrew}} were casting a net into the sea.
{{Abraham}} took {{Isaac}}, his only son, whom he loved, up Mount Moriah.
{{David}} picked up five smooth stones and ran toward {{Goliath}}.
{{Ruth}} said to {{Naomi}}, Where you go I will go.
{{Elijah}} sat down under a broom tree and asked that he might die.
{{Martha}} was distracted with much serving, but {{Mary}} sat at the feet of {{Jesus}}.
In Acts nine, {{Saul}} is on the road to Damascus.
{{Jacob}} wrestled with the angel all night long at Peniel.
{{Joseph}} said to his brothers, You meant it for evil but God meant it for good.
{{Hannah}} prayed so hard that {{Eli}} thought she was drunk.
{{Jesus}} said to {{Thomas}}, Stop doubting and believe.
{{Nehemiah}} rebuilt the wall in fifty two days.
{{Zacchaeus}} was a wee little man and he climbed up in a sycamore tree.
{{Barnabas}} took {{John Mark}} and sailed to Cyprus.
{{Samuel}} anointed {{David}}, the youngest son of {{Jesse}}.
When {{Daniel}} heard the decree was signed, he went home and prayed three times a day.
Look at Romans eight twenty eight with me.
{{Simon Peter}} drew his sword and cut off the ear of {{Malchus}}.
{{Esther}} said, If I perish, I perish.
{{Matthew}} was a tax collector before {{Jesus}} called him.
{{Rebekah}} loved {{Jacob}} but {{Isaac}} loved {{Esau}}.
{{Lazarus}} had been in the tomb four days when {{Jesus}} arrived.
The prophet {{Nathan}} looked at {{David}} and said, You are the man.
{{Priscilla}} and {{Aquila}} took {{Apollos}} aside and explained the way of God more accurately.
{{James}}, the brother of our Lord, wrote that faith without works is dead.
{{Elizabeth}} was filled with the Holy Spirit when {{Mary}} greeted her.
{{Gideon}} put out a fleece, and then he put out another one.
{{Stephen}} saw the heavens opened as they stoned him.
{{Paul}} and {{Silas}} were singing hymns at midnight in the Philippian jail.
Grace is not something you earn, it is something you receive.
Mark my words, the Lord will provide.
Will you trust him when it doesn't make sense?
Hope deferred makes the heart sick, says Proverbs thirteen.
{{Noah}} built the ark when there wasn't a cloud in the sky.
Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
{{John Wesley}} felt his heart strangely warmed on Aldersgate Street in seventeen thirty eight.
{{Charles Spurgeon}} preached to thousands at the Metropolitan Tabernacle.
{{Martin Luther}} nailed the ninety five theses to the door at Wittenberg.
{{George Whitefield}} could be heard by thirty thousand people in an open field.
{{Jonathan Edwards}} preached Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God in Enfield.
{{Hudson Taylor}} adopted Chinese dress to reach the people of the interior.
{{William Carey}} said, Expect great things from God, attempt great things for God.
{{Amy Carmichael}} rescued children from temple slavery in India.
{{Corrie ten Boom}} forgave the guard from Ravensbruck.
{{Fanny Crosby}} wrote over eight thousand hymns, and she was blind.
{{Augustine}} said our hearts are restless until they rest in you.
{{Calvin}} and {{Zwingli}} disagreed about the Lord's Supper.
{{D. L. Moody}} was a shoe salesman before he was a preacher.
{{Wesley}} rode two hundred and fifty thousand miles on horseback.
{{Spurgeon}} struggled with depression most of his life.
{{Billy Graham}} held a crusade in Charlotte in nineteen forty seven.
{{Jim Elliot}} and four other missionaries were killed by the Waodani in nineteen fifty six.
{{Elisabeth Elliot}} went back to live among the people who killed her husband.
{{Dietrich Bonhoeffer}} was hanged at Flossenburg just weeks before the war ended.
{{Polycarp}} said, Eighty six years I have served him and he has done me no wrong.
{{Francis Asbury}} brought Methodism across the American frontier.
{{Susanna Wesley}} spent an hour each week with each of her children.
{{Charles Wesley}} wrote And Can It Be and O for a Thousand Tongues.
{{William Tyndale}} was strangled and burned for translating the Bible into English.
{{Athanasius}} stood against the world for the deity of Christ.
{{Lottie Moon}} gave her food away and starved in China.
{{Adoniram Judson}} spent seventeen months in a Burmese prison.
{{John Newton}} was a slave trader before he wrote Amazing Grace.
{{William Wilberforce}} fought for twenty years to end the slave trade.
Mr. {{Wesley}} preached at five in the morning to the miners at Kingswood.
{{C. S. Lewis}} said that pain is God's megaphone to rouse a deaf world.
{{A. W. Tozer}} wrote that what comes into our minds when we think about God is the most important thing about us.
{{Tim Keller}} put it this way, you are more sinful than you ever dared believe.
As {{Bonhoeffer}} put it, when Christ calls a man he bids him come and die.
{{Oswald Chambers}} in My Utmost for His Highest says the same thing.
{{Max Lucado}} tells a story about a woodcarver named {{Eli}}.
{{John Piper}} says God is most glorified in us when we are most satisfied in him.
{{Charles Stanley}} used to say obey God and leave all the consequences to him.
{{John Bunyan}} wrote Pilgrim's Progress from the Bedford jail.
{{Thomas}} a {{Kempis}} wrote The Imitation of Christ.
{{Blaise Pascal}} talked about a God shaped vacuum in every heart.
{{Abraham Lincoln}} said he had been driven many times to his knees.
{{Matthew Henry}} commented that the woman was taken out of man's side to be equal with him.
{{Watchman Nee}} wrote The Normal Christian Life from prison.
{{Philip Yancey}} asks what's so amazing about grace.
Brother {{Lawrence}} practiced the presence of God while washing dishes.
{{Elisabeth Elliot}} said the secret is Christ in me, not me in a different set of circumstances.
{{Martin Luther King}} said the time is always right to do what is right.
{{Ravi Zacharias}} used to talk about the four questions every worldview must answer.
{{Richard Baxter}} said I preached as never sure to preach again, and as a dying man to dying men.
{{Thomas Watson}} said, the godly man is a mourner for sin.
{{Andrew Murray}} wrote a little book called Humility.
{{Spurgeon}} once told his students, a sermon without Christ is like bread without flour.
{{Lewis}} called it the weight of glory.
